questions.mathsCheckpoint: 2x^3-24x^2+40x = 2x(x-2)(x-10); scheme B1M1A1 and alternative via (x-2) or (x-10) agree.
Integral = x^5/5 - 4x^(3/2) - 3x + c; scheme cao requires +c.
x ln3 = y ln7 so x/y = ln7/ln3 = log_3 7 (about 1.7712).
1-(1-2x^2)^2 = 4x^2-4x^4; divided by (x/3)(x/2) gives 24-24x^2; exact limit as x->0 is 24.
Quotient 3x-2, remainder -x-17; A=3, B=-2, C=4, D=-5.
N(3) = 1007; T = ln(5/2)/0.075 = 12.22; dN/dt at t=3 = 299.4 cars per month; refinement replaces 5000 by 6500.
f(1)=3, f(-1)=11; gf(x) >= 7; no intersections for -4 <= k < -5/3 (vertex line k=-5/3; parallel branch k=-4).
Six solutions per 2pi requires n = 3; sin^2(3x)=k^2 has 6 solutions per pi, so 30 in 0 <= x < 5pi (numerically confirmed).
AD = 6a+(3-k)b parallel to 15a-5b gives k=5; solving 4lambda = -2+5mu, -5lambda = -3+2mu gives lambda=1/3, so BX:XD = 1:2.
f'(x) = 2x(x^2-3)/(1+x^2)^3; P = (-sqrt3, -1/8); x=tan(theta) gives cos2theta with alpha=-pi/4, beta=pi/4; area R = 1.
